messages.subject: Re: How to observe individual input elements which were created in bulk in R Shiny
parts:
You can use [[-style indexing to dynamically access an input name, e.g.:

val <- input[[paste0('column', i)]]

If you want one observe() per input, you can do that by putting observe() inside the body of an lapply.


# in server.R server function
maxIdSeen <- 0
observe({
  if (!is.null(input$numCols) && input$numCols > maxIdSeen) {
    on.exit(maxIdSeen <<- input$numCols)
    lapply(maxIdSeen+1:input$numCols, function(i) {
      observe({
        val <- input[[paste0("column", i)]]
        # do something with val
      })
    })
  }
})

messages.subject: Re: How to observe individual input elements which were created in bulk in R Shiny
parts:
The context is a set of data frames each having n rows x m columns.
Data can be simulated as:
global.R
data1 <- t(combn(20, 4))    #numCols is 4
data2 <- t(comb(25, 6))      #numCols is 6
data3 <- t(combn(15, 5))    #numCols is 5
data4 <- t(combn(30, 5))    #numCols is 5


Use selects the data frame name via:
 ui.R
      selectInput(
        inputId = "dataName",
        label   = "Select your data",
        choices = c("data1", "data2", "data3", "data4")
      )

The number of columns is variable and is is determined at server.R from the name of the data selected by the user at ui.R from the above sliderInput.
As soon as the data name is determined and implicitly the number of columns via function numCols(), a number of sliderInput is created, one for each column.
server.R

    output$sliders <- renderUI({
      numSliders <- numCols(input$dataName)
      lapply(1:numSliders, function(i) {
        sliderInput(
                    inputId = paste0('column', i),
                    label = paste0('Select the range for column ', i),
                    min = min(selectRange(input$dataName)),
                    max = max(selectRange(input$dataName)),
                    value = c(min(selectRange(input$dataName)), max(selectRange(input$dataName))),
                    step =1)
        })
    })


All sliders are presented at ui.R side by:
ui.R
uiOutput(outputId = "sliders")

At this point, user can select the range of numbers for each columns of data by changing the range from the corresponding sliderInput.
The output should change according to the ranges set by the user in via one or more sliderInput widgets.
Therefore, the application is a filtering type of app.

Thank you,
I.
